mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen every week for the last four weeks (-22.7 to -50.1). This monotonic downward trend reflects an ongoing contraction in discretionary mobility that is likely to persist mechanically into the next period absent a policy reversal, producing a further decline in mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days despite no observed deceleration in the weekly rate of RETAIL_REC decline.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in WORKPLACES mobility below -50 percent from baseline indicates binding stay-at-home/work-from-home policy enforcement that suppresses commute-linked retail trips, causing RETAIL_REC to decline further over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -50 percent from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks even though WORKPLACES remains below -50 percent.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous steep declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES jointly remove both the commute trigger and the physical transit access that enable incidental retail visits, creating a compounding suppression effect on RETAIL_REC beyond what either series would predict alone, over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -73.6 and WORKPLACES at -56.3 at t-0w, both declining weekly
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 28 days is no steeper than predicted by either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: Under an active Stage-3-style lockdown regime, PARKS mobility co-moves with RETAIL_REC because outdoor leisure trips and nearby retail/food stops are jointly curtailed by movement restrictions; the sharp PARKS decline (-26.4 to -42.6) signals continued suppression of linked retail activity over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -26.4 to -42.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks while PARKS continues to decline, breaking the assumed co-movement.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM crossing from positive to negative territory (8.0 at t-3w to -22.1 at t-0w) signals the end of initial panic-buying behavior and a shift toward minimal essential-only trips, which precedes a further one-week contraction in broader RETAIL_REC as households settle into reduced-mobility routines.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses below 0 percent from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from +8.0 to -22.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat in the week immediately following GROCERY_PHARM's crossing below zero.

mechanism_narrative: The widening gap between rising RESIDENTIAL (10.3 to 24.3) and falling WORKPLACES/RETAIL_REC indicates an entrenched stay-home behavioral pattern; as RESIDENTIAL continues to climb, it mechanically signals continued time spent at home at the expense of retail outings, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose every week from 10.3 to 24.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its upward trajectory.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and PARKS simultaneously post week-on-week declines exceeding 10 points, it indicates an acute tightening of movement restrictions that will suppress RETAIL_REC sharply within the following week, as the two series jointly capture both transit-based and outdoor-based access channels to retail destinations.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and PARKS both fall more than 10 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 20.5 points and TRANSIT fell 5.3 points between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a joint TRANSIT/PARKS drop exceeding the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: In a sustained lockdown regime, the seasonal/behavioral floor effect means RETAIL_REC decline decelerates as it approaches a structural lower bound (comparable to extreme suppression seen in TRANSIT near -73.6); as remaining discretionary trips are already minimized, further four-week decline should flatten rather than deepen.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly decline decelerated from -21.4 to -4.0 points between consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline at an accelerating or constant rate over the next 28 days rather than flattening or reversing.
